messages:
alex: Noticed two incidents where admission accepted requests and later the runtime couldn't allocate the slot -> double-alloc risk. Happened across region failover windows. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: Yep, reproduced locally when soft-slot admit is separate from final allocation. Replica A admits then replica B also admits before either reaches the allocator. We end up overcommitting.

samir: Can you drop the policy snippet and the exact ordering you hit? Might be a race in admit->check-occupancy->allocate.

maria: Snippet (simplified):
```
policy admit_if tenant_quota > 0
score = 0.6*cost_rank + 0.4*latency_rank
on_no_capacity: fallback(region="eu-west-1", tier="burst")
```
Flow: admit -> return tentative_route -> runtime alloc attempt -> fail -> fallback. The tentative_route isn't reserved until allocation.

jia: A couple options: (1) Make admit atomic with reservation (strong lock), (2) Issue ephemeral admission tokens that must be presented during allocation (single-use), (3) Shard admission by (tenant, route) so only one replica can admit that key.

alex: Strong locks solve correctness but hurt p99. Tokens add one extra roundtrip for alloc confirm but are lightweight. Sharding is fast but adds hotspots. Tradeoffs?

samir: Metrics to measure before picking: admit_conflicts/s, token_failures, avg_token_latency, hot_shard_qps. Also simulate 5-10% hot tenants at 20k qps.

maria: I prototyped tokens: runtime issues admit_token and stores it in a short-lived memstore. Alloc must supply token; token is invalidated on use. Token TTL tested at 150ms worked well.

jia: Edge case: if token TTL expires due to GC or network pause, alloc will fail and trigger fallback -> can increase fallback churn. We should emit token_expiry_rate and consider jittering TTL by request size. Also include region-affinity TTL on fallbacks to avoid oscillation.

alex: Proposal: add admit_token primitive to the policy DSL (opt-in). Default behavior unchanged. Plan: policy-engine v2 implements token + optimistic CAS hybrid. Rollout: canary, telemetry gating, kill-switch.

samir: Also consider a fallback-serialization hint in the DSL: on_no_capacity: serialized_fallback(ttl=30s) so runtime won't immediately flip between regions on retries.

maria: I'll add a simulator to policy-engine tests to model concurrent admits and token expiry. Will run at 10k qps with 10% hot tenants.

jia: I'll sketch the runtime API: IssueToken(tenant, route) -> token; ConfirmAlloc(token) -> ok/expired. We'll need to spec retries and error codes.

alex: Assign follow-ups: @maria sim + tests, @samir dash for token metrics and shard heatmap, @jia runtime API impl, I'll write RFC with proto changes and rollout checklist.

ops-bot: Heads up: staging cluster saw +2% admission retries since 02:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: policy-engine v2 canary started (staging) - 3/3 pods healthy

alex: Sync Friday architecture meeting to finalize RFC and canary thresholds. Thanks all.
